messages:
Sam (Sales): Hey team — Auriga banking POC kicks off tomorrow. They want Redwood Private with strict egress through their on-prem TLS-inspecting proxy. Main asks: PrivateLink vs VPC peering tradeoffs, required firewall rules, and any pricing delta for PrivateLink + proxy. Can we sync today?
Priya (Solutions Engineer): Quick background from the customer: regulated, no direct internet egress from their VPC. Preferred pattern is customer-managed egress/proxy. They asked if we can accept connections from a PrivateLink endpoint in their VPC or if peering is simpler.
Miguel (NetEng): Short answer: both can work but different constraints. PrivateLink (AWS VPCE) -> we terminate on an NLB inside our VPC and traffic stays private; it's compatible with customer forcing traffic through their egress proxy. VPC peering is L3 routing, simpler for some teams but you can't force traffic through their NAT/proxy if the customer doesn't change route tables.
Priya (Solutions Engineer): They specifically said they need TLS inspection on outbound and also want to record source IPs for audits. Any concerns there?
Miguel (NetEng): Two notes: 1) Source IP preservation — PrivateLink will NAT at the endpoint (the interface endpoint's ENI) so original source IP is not preserved to our pods by default. If they need source IPs preserved end-to-end for audit, peering or a direct routing path that maintains source IP is better. 2) If they want all egress inspected, best is: customer routes outbound to their proxy, proxy does inspection, then proxy initiates connections to our VPCE/NLB. That matches PrivateLink well (customer initiates).
Jia (Security): Also need to call out mutual TLS + client auth. For a bank we require mTLS on the connection from their proxy to our endpoint and cert-based auth for the admin APIs. We'll need their CA bundle or they'll use a signed cert we trust. Also need assurance on logging retention and access controls.
Alex (Pricing): Pricing tradeoffs: PrivateLink itself has per-hour/VPCE-hour and per-GB data processing (AWS charges) + our traffic egress bills. VPC peering has no VPCE processing fee but may incur cross-AZ/data transfer costs depending on topology. For a POC scale (low TB), VPCE running cost will be small but for production we should model expected monthly TB. Rough ballpark: AWS VPCE data processing ~ $0.01–0.02/GB (varies), plus our standard outbound egress pricing. I'll run detailed calc if you share expected GB/day.
Sam (Sales): They asked about firewall rules — minimal list we should give them to hand to their netops. Can you draft a short allowlist?
Miguel (NetEng): Draft firewall snippets below — these are minimal and assume PrivateLink interface endpoints in customer VPC talking to our NLB. They'll replace <VPCE-IPs> with the actual ENI IPs and we'll provide final list once endpoint is provisioned.
Miguel (NetEng): ```
# Customer egress proxy -> Redwood PrivateLink (recommended)
# Allow outbound from proxy -> destination TCP/443 to <redwood-vpce-ips-or-dns>
ALLOW OUT tcp 443 to <redwood_vpce_ips_or_dns>

# Health checks (if we ask) - optional
ALLOW OUT tcp 443 to <redwood_health_check_ips>

# If using VPC peering + NAT
# Allow outbound from application subnet -> TCP/443 to 0.0.0.0/0 (proxied via customer's NAT/proxy)
ALLOW OUT tcp 443 to 0.0.0.0/0 via <customer-proxy-ip>
```
Priya (Solutions Engineer): They also want an example for an ACL on the Redwood side (they asked about source IP expectations). What do we provide?
Miguel (NetEng): We can provide stable egress ranges for our side if they request allowlisting for return paths (eg, monitoring, callbacks). For PrivateLink the connection is customer-initiated so we don't need to open inbound from the internet. For peering, route tables control reachability. We'll provide a short list like: [redwood-vpc-egress-range-1, redwood-vpc-egress-range-2] once env created.
Jia (Security): Checklist for them:
- mTLS active between their proxy and our endpoint (client certs)
- TLS versions >= 1.2, prefer 1.3
- Client cert rotation window (we recommend 90 days)
- Audit logs retained 365 days for POI (we can discuss retention tiers)
- No plaintext health endpoints over public internet

Sam (Sales): Customer also worried about IP preservation for fraud logs. They said their backend ties sessions to original source IP. How do we address?
Miguel (NetEng): If their backend needs the original client IP in the request, options:
- Use VPC peering (source IP preserved).
- If PrivateLink is mandatory, have the customer's proxy inject X-Forwarded-For with original IP and ensure we pass that to their app (but they must trust that header — audit implications).
- VPN with policy-based routes that preserve IP.
Choose based on their security posture.
Priya (Solutions Engineer): Customer also asked if Redwood can support a TLS-inspecting forward proxy hosted on their side (i.e., they terminate/re-sign and then outbound to Redwood). They want to ensure content filtering. This is compatible with PrivateLink as Miguel said, since the customer initiates connection from their proxy to our interface endpoint.
Alex (Pricing): One more pricing note — if they want Dedicated (reserved capacity) for lower latency and predictable throughput, that adds a fixed instance/hour cost plus networking. Recommend we scope POC on hosted private with VPCE, then model Dedicated if throughput grows. I'll prepare a 3-month POC price sheet.
Sam (Sales): Great. Can we capture action items?
Miguel (NetEng): Action: Provide final firewall allowlist + sample SG/ACL (owner: Miguel) — ETA EOD today.
Jia (Security): Action: Send mTLS cert requirements + JWKS/CA format and recommended rotation (owner: Jia) — ETA tomorrow morning.
Alex (Pricing): Action: Price sheet for VPCE + Dedicated delta for expected 1TB/mo (owner: Alex) — ETA EOD today.
Priya (Solutions Engineer): Action: Ask customer whether they require source IP preservation or if XFF header is acceptable (owner: Priya) — I'm doing this now.
deploy-bot: New POC workspace created: workspace-id=auriga-poc-22345, assigned to Sam.
Sam (Sales): Thanks all — I'll consolidate and send to Auriga after we have Miguel's SG/ACL and Jia's cert notes. @Priya ping me as soon as you hear about IP preservation. :thumbsup:
